evals.prompt: Read the approved spec, handoff, stale notes, source, exports, callers, and tests. Use Definition Mode to produce a codebase design for sync preview. Do not implement or write a plan.
evals.expected_output: A compact definition artifact with exact repository-native declarations, shared plan ownership, preview and execution interaction, caller knowledge, and short Tech Notes without function bodies.
assertions: Grounds the current model in actual modules and public exports
Makes shared filtering and ordering ownership explicit
Explains preview and execution control/data flow and client avoidance
Keeps dry-run, stdout formatting, mode flags, and callbacks out of syncSessions by sharing the ordered plan as data
Uses exact repository-native declarations plus 2-3 line Tech Notes for non-obvious semantics
Uses ASCII for every interaction or dependency diagram
Rejects stale command, plugin, config, and TypeScript proposals
Contains no full function implementation

Explains preview and execution interaction through one charge-plan policy

evals.prompt: In Definition Mode, revise the existing sync-preview design after this human correction: SyncPlanner must be an independent logical module because a future scheduled job is a third caller. The CLI and sync executor both consume plan(records). The planner knows nothing about stdout or the client. Public exports remain unchanged. Do not implement code or write a plan.
evals.expected_output: A revised declaration-first architecture model that applies the corrected module and exact interface without reopening alternatives, inventing rationale, or specifying unconfirmed scheduled-job behavior.
assertions: Uses an independent SyncPlanner with the exact plan(records) interface
Makes CLI and executor consume the planner without planner I/O knowledge
Preserves existing public exports
Does not reopen the corrected choice with alternatives or retroactive rationale
Does not invent scheduled-job execution behavior
Contains no full function implementation

evals.prompt: Use Audit Mode to review the complete billing-preview fixture repository. Find material over-abstraction, coupling, leaky boundaries, or dead legacy design. Do not implement or write a migration plan.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-ranked findings that distinguish real current boundaries from stale proposals, show smaller exact target contracts or deletions, and end with a compact dependency shape.
assertions: Scans exports, callers, tests, and dependency direction across the fixture
Ranks only material findings and cites paths or symbols
Does not report stale-notes proposals as live architecture
Shows an exact smaller target contract or deletion for each finding
Uses ASCII for every target module or dependency diagram
Uses Tech Notes only for non-obvious effect, failure, state, transaction, or concurrency semantics
Contains no implementation or rollout plan

evals.prompt: Read the approved spec, handoff, stale notes, source, callers, and tests. Use Definition Mode to produce a codebase design for reliable approval notification delivery. Do not implement or write a plan.
evals.expected_output: A language-native architecture artifact that explains the end-to-end approval and delivery shape before giving exact load-bearing contracts, with explicit transaction ownership, retry semantics, stable delivery identity, and hidden persistence/provider details.
assertions: Traces both approval callers through one domain capability and preserves Service.Approve
Shows the complete approval-to-delivery dependency and interaction shape before local declaration detail
Assigns atomic order update and notification intent persistence to one explicit transaction owner
Explains worker retry after send or acknowledgement failure using one stable delivery identity
Keeps database rows and provider payloads behind load-bearing repository and notification boundaries
Avoids a global ports package, temporal worker stages, direct caller notification, and speculative infrastructure
Keeps every interaction flow consistent with preserved and proposed signatures
Uses exact repository-native contracts without full implementations or a file-by-file inventory
